newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialist ex-minister jailed for sleaze.
newsitem.headline: French Socialist ex-minister jailed for sleaze.

text.p: A French court on Tuesday jailed former Socialist junior minister Jean-Michel Boucheron for two years, with another two suspended, and fined him one million francs ($172,000) for taking bribes from companies bidding in public tenders.

Boucheron, an ex-minister for territorial administration and the former mayor of the southwestern town of Angouleme, returned three months ago from Argentina to face sleaze charges at home after six years on the run in South America.
The Paris court found him guilty of taking bribes worth about 550,000 francs ($100,000) in 1986-89 from various companies.
It said he also received fees of 327,000 francs ($55,000) for a fictitious job by Compagnie Generale des Eaux in exchange for giving the utility a water distribution contract in Angouleme.
Boucheron, 50, had been tried in his absence and sentenced to four years in jail but was entitled to a re-trial under French law.

The former mayor fled to Uruguay in 1991 as magistrates investigated a gaping deficit in municipal finances. He went on to open a restaurant in the Argentine capital, Buenos Aires, that eventually went bankrupt.
Following a French extradition request, he was held for three weeks in Argentina in 1995 and released on $50,000 bail.
Another French politician, ex-mayor of Nice Jacques Medecin, fled to Uruguay in the early 1990s. He was later extradited and served two years in prison on fraud charges.

A former schoolteacher, Boucheron was elected mayor of Angouleme in 1977 and entered parliament the following year. His political career collapsed soon after reaching its peak in 1988, when he was a member of the cabinet for just one month.

An unemployed taxpayer in Angouleme was the first to publicly accuse him of suspected fraud. Boucheron was defeated in a 1989 municipal election. Angouleme is still paying a 164-million franc ($28 million) bill for his stint as mayor.
